Question: An isosceles trapezoid is circumscribed around a circle. The longer base of the trapezoid is \(16,\) and one of the base angles is \(\arcsin(0.8).\) Find the area of the trapezoid.
Solution:
Tangency relates the four side lengths, while the base angle relates a leg to the height and the difference of the bases.

Let the shorter base be \(b\), each leg have length \(\ell\), and the height be \(h\). Set \(\theta=\arcsin(0.8)\). This principal angle is acute, so it is an angle at the longer base, and
\[
\sin\theta=\frac45,\qquad
\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}=\frac35.
\]
From each vertex, the two tangent segments to the circle have equal lengths. Each sum of opposite sides therefore contains the same four vertex contributions. In particular,
\[
16+b=2\ell.
\]
Drop perpendiculars from the endpoints of the shorter base to the longer base. The two resulting right triangles have equal hypotenuses and equal heights, so they are congruent. Each horizontal leg has length \((16-b)/2\). Hence
\[
h=\ell\sin\theta=\frac45\ell,
\qquad
16-b=2\ell\cos\theta=\frac65\ell.
\]
Adding the two equations involving \(b\) eliminates it:
\[
32=2\ell+\frac65\ell=\frac{16}{5}\ell.
\]
Thus \(\ell=10\), so \(b=4\) and \(h=8\). These give positive bases with \(b<16\), as required. The area is
\[
\frac{16+b}{2}h
=\frac{16+4}{2}\cdot8
=\boxed{80},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
